title: Horizontal graph keeps dragging state after clicking nodes or labels

evidence.quote: drag.current is initialized on pointer down and only cleared by endDrag.
Branch-label pointer-up stops propagation before the parent endDrag handler can run.
Node pointer-up stops propagation before the parent endDrag handler can run.

reasoning: Clicking a graph node or branch label bubbles pointerdown to the scroll container, setting drag.current. The child pointerup then calls stopPropagation, so the container's onPointerUp=endDrag never runs and drag.current remains non-null. Subsequent pointermove events over the graph, even with no button pressed, satisfy the onPointerMove guard and can unexpectedly scroll/pan the graph or mark the next click as moved.
reproduction: Render HorizontalBranchGraph, click a node without dragging, keep the cursor over the graph, then move the mouse. The scroll container can pan because drag.current still contains the click origin.
recommendation: Clear drag state on child pointer-up after handling selection, or avoid stopping propagation and let the parent endDrag run. Also guard onPointerMove with e.buttons so stale drag state cannot pan after the button is released.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked tests exercise core diff and branch storage behavior only; @docgit/ui has no real interaction tests for pointer drag/click behavior.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a UI interaction test for HorizontalBranchGraph that clicks a node, dispatches a pointermove with no pressed buttons, and asserts scrollLeft/scrollTop and panning state do not change.
